paras_en: On November 5, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – Luxury apparel brand Ralph Lauren (RL-US) lifted its revenue and operating margin outlook for fiscal 2027, but its third‑quarter revenue growth forecast remains below Wall Street expectations. Strong demand in North America and Asia continues, yet it is insufficient to dispel concerns about short‑term growth slowing, and the stock fell about 7% in pre‑market trading after the earnings release.

The company projects third‑quarter revenue to rise 3%‑4% year‑over‑year, below analysts’ 4.2% estimate, mainly due to slower wholesale shipment timing and reduced sales through discount channels. In contrast, the full‑year revenue growth outlook was raised from 5%‑6% to 6%‑7%; after excluding currency effects, the full‑year operating margin is expected to improve by 0.8 to 1 percentage point, better than the prior estimate of a 0.6‑0.8 point gain.

Second‑quarter revenue grew 9% year‑over‑year to $2.19 billion, topping the market forecast of $2.12 billion, and adjusted earnings per share were $4.64, exceeding the expected $4.26. Revenue in China surged 35%, becoming a key growth driver, while demand from high‑income U.S. consumers for knit sweaters and polo shirts supported the company’s performance, which has outpaced the broader luxury sector in recent quarters.

Ralph Lauren has recently increased the share of premium apparel and refreshed its product mix to improve sales. This outlook shows continued improvement in full‑year growth and profitability, though quarterly revenue remains vulnerable to channel and shipment timing. The stock had risen about 16% up to the prior trading day, reflecting investors’ high expectations for rapid growth, which magnifies the gap between the Q3 guidance and market forecasts.

items.title: 美國上周初領失業金人數降至18.9萬 追平57年低點
items.title_en: U.S. Initial Unemployment Claims Drop to 189,000 Last Week, Tying 57-Year Low
paras: 美國上周初領失業救濟金人數降至18.9萬人，追平1969年以來最低紀錄，顯示企業裁員仍少，勞動市場維持韌性。不過，續領人數回升，加上企業新增招募多為季節性職缺，反映「低招募、低裁員」格局尚未打破，就業穩定未必意味求職更容易。
美國勞工部周四(5日)公布，截至10月31日當周，經季節調整後初領人數減少6,000人，低於分析師預估的19.6萬人。前一周數據上修至19.5萬人，本次則追平7月中旬的18.9萬人，為57年低點。

初領低檔不等於就業熱絡 招募仍偏保守

初領人數自9月中旬以來多數低於20萬人。強勁內需與獲利成長讓企業傾向留住員工，但美國、以色列與伊朗戰爭持續，帶來的不確定性仍抑制招募。
9月每名失業者對應的職缺數，由8月的1.02個升至1.06個，部分經濟學家視為勞動市場開始趨緊的訊號。不過，也有人認為，初領偏低可能反映移民管制使勞動人口縮減，不能全歸因於裁員減少。
Challenger公布，企業10月宣布裁員43,994人，月增2%，年減71%，為2023年以來最低的10月水準。同月招募計畫達444,692人，年增57%，創2009年以來同期最高，但可能多為季節性工作。
該公司營收長Andy Challenger表示，企業希望保留既有員工，並透過短期人力滿足假期需求，避免增加永久編制。

續領回升凸顯求職困境 非農報告周五登場

截至10月24日當周，續領失業救濟金人數增加2.3萬人，至171.8萬人。雖仍處低檔，但企業不願擴大長期招募，意味部分失業者可能更難找到下一份工作。
續領數據也無法涵蓋所有失業者，例如缺乏工作經歷的應屆畢業生，或已領完救濟金者。多數州給付期限為26周，因此低續領人數不宜直接解讀為失業問題輕微。
民眾感受也未隨低裁員改善。密西根大學10月消費者信心指數為48，仍接近歷史低檔，反映購買力與物價壓力持續影響家庭信心。
市場接著關注周五10月非農就業報告。《路透》調查預估新增就業6.5萬人，高於9月的2.9萬人，失業率料維持4.2%。不過，本次初領數據落在非農調查期間之外，無法直接用來判斷該份報告結果。
paras_en: Initial claims for unemployment benefits in the United States fell to 189,000 last week, matching the lowest level since 1969, indicating that corporate layoffs remain limited and the labor market stays resilient. However, continued claims rose and most new hires are seasonal, showing that the "low hiring, low layoffs" pattern has not broken and job stability does not necessarily mean it is easier to find work.

The Labor Department announced on Thursday, the 5th, that for the week ending October 31, seasonally adjusted initial claims decreased by 6,000 to 189,000, below analysts' forecast of 196,000. The prior week’s figure had been revised up to 195,000, and this release ties the mid‑July level of 189,000, the lowest since 1957.

Low initial claims do not equal a hot job market; hiring remains cautious. Initial claims have mostly stayed under 200,000 since mid‑September. Strong domestic demand and profit growth lead firms to retain staff, but ongoing wars involving the U.S., Israel and Iran keep uncertainty high and suppress hiring.

The ratio of job openings to unemployed rose from 1.02 in August to 1.06 in September, which some economists view as a sign the labor market is tightening. Others caution that the low initial claim number may also reflect a shrinking labor force due to immigration restrictions, not solely fewer layoffs.

Challenger reported that companies announced 43,994 layoffs in October, a 2% month‑over‑month increase but a 71% year‑over‑year decline, the lowest October level since 2023. In the same month, hiring plans reached 444,692, up 57% year‑over‑year and the highest since 2009, though many of these jobs are likely seasonal.
Andy Challenger, the company’s revenue chief, said firms want to keep existing employees and meet holiday demand with short‑term labor, avoiding the addition of permanent positions.

Continuing claims rose by 23,000 to 1.718 million for the week ending October 24. Although still low, firms’ reluctance to expand long‑term hiring suggests some unemployed may find it harder to secure their next job.

Continuing‑claim data also miss many jobless, such as recent graduates lacking work experience or those who have exhausted their benefits. Most states cap benefits at 26 weeks, so low continuing claims should not be taken as evidence that unemployment problems are minor.

Consumer sentiment has not improved with the drop in layoffs. The University of Michigan’s October consumer confidence index was 48, still near historic lows, reflecting ongoing pressure on purchasing power and prices that dampen household confidence.

Markets now turn to Friday’s October non‑farm payroll report. Reuters polls project 65,000 new jobs, up from September’s 29,000, with the unemployment rate expected to hold at 4.2%. However, the initial‑claim figures fall outside the payroll survey period and cannot be used directly to gauge that report’s outcome.

items.title: 美國「藍潮」恐限制AI投資？高盛認為反而會加速
items.title_en: U.S. ‘Blue Wave’ May Threaten AI Investment? Goldman Sachs Says It Could Actually Accelerate It
paras: 美國期中選舉「藍色浪潮」席捲國會兩院，市場擔憂民主黨加強AI監管，將拖慢資料中心擴張。不過，高盛歐洲股票交易主管普里沃羅茨基（Rich Privorotsky）提出相反看法，認為科技巨頭可能趕在政策調整前提前投入資金，推動AI資本支出加速，既有算力資產也可望受惠。
普里沃羅茨基在周三(4日)發布的研報指出，近幾周AI類股持續遭到拋售，估值已回落，空頭部位也有回補需求。選舉結果未必會抑制資本投入，反而可能促使企業加快布局。
德州州長選舉是市場關注焦點，因為全美約四分之一規劃中的資料中心位於該州。共和黨籍現任州長阿博特（Greg Abbott）敗給民主黨候選人伊諾霍薩（Gina Hinojosa），被外界解讀為當地AI監管可能收緊，雲端巨頭投資步伐恐放緩。
但普里沃羅茨基認為，科技企業決策者可能將資本投入提前至2027年，趁規劃政策調整前，利用現行審批條件完成策略性交易。
他也指出，2029年新總統上任後，可能推動稅制調整、加強行政監管與併購審查。在此背景下，大型雲端業者可能進一步加快布局。
擴建受限 既有算力反而更值錢
普里沃羅茨基提出另一個觀點：若未來算力擴充受到限制，已投產、可供使用的算力資產，價值反而可能提高。
理論上，這將有利於亞馬遜(AMZN-US) 、微軟(MSFT-US) 及Alphabet(GOOGL-US) 等已部署大量算力的雲端巨頭。即使新增供給受限，業者手中的既有資產仍可能受惠。
不過，Nebius(YNDX-US) 、CoreWeave(CRWV-US) 等新興雲端服務商的情況較複雜。投資判斷很大程度取決於其算力資源是否已簽訂長期合約，以及是否擁有足夠的自有算力，不能一概而論。
供應鏈仍有風險 估值已先修正
普里沃羅茨基坦言，部分資料中心專案未來可能延後或擱置，進而拖累所謂「賣鏟人」行情，包括晶片、冷卻與電力設備廠商，以及能源服務商。
不過，相關類股先前已經歷一波修正。例如費城半導體指數ETF過去一個月跌幅達兩成，他認為後續下跌空間可能有限。
他並以AMD(AMD-US) 第三季亮眼業績，說明AI資本支出週期仍具韌性。AMD在3日盤後提出優於市場預期的第四季展望，預估2027年營收成長率將超過80%，伺服器CPU營收可望翻倍。
普里沃羅茨基認為，晶片供給受限不會讓需求消失，反而可能讓高價維持更久。即使資料中心建置延後，導致雲端業者先前訂單高於實際需求，這項風險也已反映在目前偏低的估值中。
選舉不確定性消退 有利股市回穩
除了產業基本面，普里沃羅茨基也關注選後市場情緒。他認為，隨著期中選舉塵埃落定、不確定性下降，VIX恐慌指數很難持續維持目前的高檔水準。
若市場波動率如他預期快速回落，考量波動率與股指呈負相關，美股主要指數將有望上行。
普里沃羅茨基在研報中形容，AI個股已遭拋售至超跌。他認為，相關企業基本面依然強勁，選舉帶來的不確定性已消退，持倉結構也較先前改善；監管可能收緊，未必就代表AI投資將立即降溫。
paras_en: The U.S. midterm election’s “blue wave” swept both chambers of Congress, prompting market worries that a Democratic push for tighter AI regulation could slow data‑center expansion. However, Rich Privorotsky, head of European equity trading at Goldman Sachs, offered a contrary view, arguing that tech giants may front‑load spending before policy changes take effect, speeding up AI capital expenditures and benefiting existing compute assets.

Privorotsky’s research note released on Wednesday (the 4th) noted that AI stocks have been sold off in recent weeks, valuations have retreated and short positions are looking to be covered. The election outcome may not curb capital deployment; instead it could prompt companies to accelerate their positioning.

The Texas governor’s race is a market focus because roughly a quarter of planned U.S. data centers are located in the state. Republican incumbent Greg Abbott’s loss to Democrat Gina Hinojosa is being read as a signal that local AI regulation could tighten, potentially slowing cloud‑provider investment pace.

Privorotsky, however, believes tech‑company decision‑makers may move capital forward to as early as 2027, taking advantage of the current approval framework to complete strategic deals before policy adjustments are implemented.

He also points out that a new president taking office in 2029 could drive tax reforms, stronger administrative oversight and tougher merger reviews. In that context, large cloud operators may further accelerate their deployments.
Expansion Constraints Make Existing Compute More Valuable
Privorotsky offers another angle: if future compute capacity expansion is limited, the value of already‑deployed, usable compute assets could actually rise.

In theory, this would benefit cloud giants such as Amazon (AMZN‑US), Microsoft (MSFT‑US) and Alphabet (GOOGL‑US), which have already deployed massive compute resources. Even if new supply is constrained, the assets they hold could still benefit.

The situation is more nuanced for emerging cloud providers like Nebius (YNDX‑US) and CoreWeave (CRWV‑US). Investment judgments will largely depend on whether their compute resources are tied to long‑term contracts and whether they have sufficient proprietary capacity, so a blanket assessment is not appropriate.
Supply‑Chain Risks Remain, Valuations Already Adjusted

Privorotsky admits that some data‑center projects may be delayed or shelved, which could weigh on the so‑called “shovel‑seller” market that includes chip, cooling and power‑equipment makers as well as energy‑service firms.

Nevertheless, related stocks have already undergone a correction. For example, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ETF fell about 20% over the past month, and he believes there is limited downside left.

He cites AMD’s (AMD‑US) strong third‑quarter results to illustrate that the AI cap‑ex cycle remains resilient. AMD posted an after‑hours outlook for Q4 that beat market expectations, forecasting revenue growth of over 80% in 2027 and a potential doubling of its server‑CPU revenue.

Privorotsky argues that constrained chip supply will not erase demand; instead it may keep prices elevated for longer. Even if data‑center builds are postponed, causing cloud providers to have orders that exceed actual demand, that risk is already reflected in today’s relatively low valuations.
Election Uncertainty Fades, Supporting Market Stabilization

Beyond industry fundamentals, Privorotsky is watching post‑election market sentiment. He believes that as the midterm dust settles and uncertainty recedes, the VIX fear index will struggle to stay at its current elevated levels.
If volatility drops as he expects, the inverse relationship between volatility and equity indices should help lift the major U.S. stock benchmarks.

Privorotsky describes AI stocks as having been sold into oversold territory in his report. He maintains that the underlying fundamentals of these companies remain strong, election‑related uncertainty has dissipated, and portfolio structures have improved; tighter regulation does not necessarily mean an immediate cooling of AI investment.

items.title: 〈美股早盤〉選後行情兩樣情！道瓊續揚、那指開低 台積電ADR挫跌4.5%
paras: 美股主要指數周四(5日)開盤漲跌不一，期中選舉後的資金輪動持續，道瓊工業指數繼前一日大漲後一度再升約300點，那斯達克指數則受晶片與資料中心相關股下跌拖累，開盤走低。
民主黨在期中選舉大勝帶動前一交易日強勁漲勢後，投資人持續轉出科技股，主要指數表現出現落差，整體市場漲勢也較前一日收斂。
截稿前，道瓊工業指數漲近130點或近0.2%，那斯達克綜合指數跌近430點或近1.7%，標普 500 指數跌近0.8%，費城半導體指數跌近5.4%，台積電ADR挫跌4.5%。
美國期中選舉帶動的資金輪動延續至第二天，投資人轉向先前失寵的市場與景氣循環股，晶片股則承受賣壓。那斯達克100指數期貨下跌0.8%，一檔追蹤美國上市晶片股的ETF盤前重挫近4%，標普500指數期貨則小漲0.1%。
市場擔心民主黨橫掃國會後，美國可能收緊資料中心監管，進而影響半導體需求。另一方面，投資人也押注財政擴張受限、中東戰爭更快落幕，有望降低能源價格與借貸成本，讓更多產業受惠。

資金轉向歐亞股市 韓系記憶體大廠重挫

歐洲Stoxx 600指數突破先前收盤高點，縮小今年以來落後標普500的差距。亞洲以中國與澳洲市場表現較強，但南韓三星電子(005930-KS)與SK海力士(SKHY-US)(000660-KS)均大跌逾7%。
Candriam多重資產主管Nadege Dufosse表示，市場假設AI資本支出放緩、伊朗戰爭落幕機率提高及能源價格下降，促使部分科技股暫歇，漲勢擴及更多類股。
黃金延續選後漲勢，每盎司突破4,100美元，前一天漲幅為8月以來最大。較低殖利率與美元走弱通常有利金價；不過，美元周四已趨穩，布蘭特原油則收復部分前一日跌幅，來到每桶97美元附近。
英國央行升息後，英國公債由漲轉跌，美債價格也走低。英國央行並暗示可能再升息，預估明年通膨將逼近5%。總裁貝里警告，中東衝突每多拖一個月，通膨壓力就持續累積。

市場押Fed下月升息 年底行情仍看AI投資

美國周四公布的上周初領失業救濟金人數低於所有市場預估，第三季生產力增幅也優於預期。投資人接著將關注周五非農就業報告，尋找經濟與利率方向線索。
貨幣市場目前預估，聯準會(Fed)下月升息1碼的機率約80%，2027年還會再升1次。
J. Safra Sarasin銀行的Wolf von Rotberg認為，選舉帶動的輪動告一段落後，市場將重新聚焦總體經濟基本面；若AI資本支出成長確實受到威脅，股市年底前恐難有好表現。
Panmure Liberum策略師Joachim Klement則表示，市場正布局延續至12月的聖誕行情，試圖逢低買進AI股。但他傾向利用年底反彈賣出，因為預期AI交易將在2027年失去動能。

Meritz表示，今年記憶體晶片訂單交付率(可供應產能與訂單量之比)一直維持在80%-85%的較低水準，推動記憶體晶片售價大幅上漲。預計2027年供需缺口將進一步擴大，訂單交付率可能降至約80%。

items.title: AI股為何殺成這樣？分析師：不只美國期中選舉 機構也在去槓桿
items.title_en: Why Are AI Stocks Plummeting? Analysts Say It's Not Just the U.S. Midterm Election—Institutions Are Also Deleveraging
paras: 美股科技股周四(5日)遭遇猛烈拋售，費城半導體指數盤中一度重挫11%，那斯達克綜合指數一度下跌5%。但在市場分析師眼中，這波跌勢不只是期中選舉後的政策疑慮，更反映投資人重新檢視AI成長預期、融資成本與投資報酬，機構減碼及去槓桿則進一步放大震盪。
據《路透》彙整，多名分析師認為，選舉是加速AI交易退潮的催化劑，問題早在財報季前浮現；也有人認為市場反應過度，資料中心業者仍可轉往海外布局，實際影響尚待觀察。

選舉只是催化劑 AI支出與報酬疑慮早已累積

瑞士銀行Swissquote資深分析師Ipek Ozkardeskaya指出，市場原本就擔心AI支出過高、借貸成本上升，以及大型雲端業者自由現金流下滑，連優於預期的財報都難以提振買氣。如今政治風險加入，使原已脆弱的信心更加承壓。
她認為，雲端業者透過增資與發債支應AI投資，正使估值面臨壓力。市場一度期待政府限制建設能替企業踩煞車，但這些公司已高度押注AI，擴張放緩也可能反過來傷害業務成長。
50 Park Investments執行長Adam Sarhan則表示，許多AI股票早已進入熊市，費半較52周高點回落約31%。投資人如今追問的是，客戶是否會持續付費，以及下一個支撐股價的利多究竟在哪裡。

資料中心監管添阻力 但海外布局仍有替代空間

Granite Wealth Management董事總經理Bruce Zaro認為，市場正重新評估選後樂觀情緒。資料中心對電網、水資源及周邊居民的影響，將帶來更多反對聲浪，尚未取得許可的計畫可能面臨更艱難的審批過程。
SimCorp投資決策研究全球主管Melissa Brown指出，新當選的國會議員與州長不太可能完全阻止AI基礎建設，但只要速度放慢，就足以引發疑慮，因為AI成長故事高度仰賴配套設施快速落地。
FHN Financial總體經濟策略師Will Compernolle則認為，地方對資料中心的反彈早已存在，選舉只是進一步確認這個趨勢。資金從晶片股轉向大型雲端業者，反映市場預期投資放緩可能減輕後者的支出壓力。
不過，Andersen Capital Management創辦人Peter Andersen認為，這波拋售缺乏充分理由。他表示，團隊訪談的資料中心建設業者指出，若美國部分地區限制興建，仍可考慮加拿大、巴西等地。投資人需要時間理解替代方案，不能立即認定需求將消失。

機構去槓桿放大跌勢 成長股轉向現金流考驗

Nationwide首席市場策略師Mark Hackett認為，這是一場情緒性拋售。財報與選舉影響雖是市場關注的理由，主要推力卻是機構積極賣出，以及避險基金和主動型機構投資人降低槓桿，尤其衝擊半導體與新型雲端等投機性較高的領域。
富國投資研究所資深全球市場策略師Sameer Samana則指出，AI股先前已反映大量成長期待，一旦成長放緩，原本追逐成長的買家可能離場，接棒者會更重視穩健現金流。
這種投資人換手需要時間，因為不少股票仍稱不上便宜。他認為，市場關鍵在於逢低買盤與重新評估長期前景的賣方，究竟誰占上風；周四的交易顯示，後者的影響更為明顯。
paras_en: U.S. tech stocks suffered a sharp sell‑off on Thursday (the 5th), with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunging as much as 11% intraday and the Nasdaq Composite falling as much as 5%. Analysts say the decline reflects not only policy uncertainty after the midterm elections but also investors reassessing AI growth expectations, financing costs and returns, while institutional trimming and deleveraging amplified the volatility.

According to a Reuters roundup, several analysts view the election as a catalyst that accelerated the retreat from AI trades, noting that concerns surfaced even before earnings season; others argue the market overreacted, pointing out that data‑center operators can still shift projects overseas, so the real impact remains to be seen.

The election is merely a catalyst—concerns about AI spending and returns have been building for a while. Swissquote senior analyst Ipek Ozkardeskaya said the market was already worried about excessive AI outlays, rising borrowing costs and declining free cash flow at large cloud providers, and even better‑than‑expected earnings could not lift sentiment. Adding political risk now further compresses already fragile confidence.

She added that cloud providers are financing AI investments through equity raises and bond issuances, putting valuation pressure on them. While the market briefly hoped that government construction limits might act as a brake, these firms are heavily bet on AI, and a slowdown in expansion could actually hurt business growth.

50 Park Investments CEO Adam Sarhan said many AI stocks have already entered a bear market, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down about 31% from its 52‑week high. Investors are now asking whether customers will keep paying and what the next catalyst to support stock prices might be.

Data‑center regulation is adding headwinds, but overseas deployment still offers alternatives. Granite Wealth Management managing director Bruce Zaro said the market is re‑evaluating post‑election optimism. The impact of data centers on power grids, water resources and nearby residents is generating more opposition, and projects without permits may face tougher approval processes.

SimCorp global head of investment decision research Melissa Brown noted that newly elected members of Congress and governors are unlikely to completely block AI infrastructure, but any slowdown in pace will raise doubts because the AI growth story relies heavily on rapid rollout of supporting facilities.

FHN Financial macro‑economics strategist Will Compernolle argued that local backlash against data centers has long existed and the election simply confirmed the trend. Capital moving from chip stocks to large cloud providers reflects expectations that a slowdown in investment could ease spending pressure on the latter.

However, Andersen Capital Management founder Peter Andersen said the sell‑off lacks sufficient justification. He cited interviews with data‑center builders who said that if construction is restricted in parts of the U.S., sites in Canada, Brazil and other regions remain viable. Investors need time to understand alternatives and cannot assume demand will vanish immediately.

Nationwide chief market strategist Mark Hackett described the move as an emotional sell‑off. While earnings and the election are cited as reasons, the main driver is aggressive selling by institutions and reduced leverage by hedge funds and active institutional investors, hitting speculative areas such as semiconductors and next‑gen cloud services the hardest.

Wells Fargo Investment Research senior global market strategist Sameer Samana pointed out that AI stocks had already priced in massive growth expectations; once growth slows, the growth‑seeking buyers may exit, leaving later entrants who prioritize solid cash flow.

This investor turnover takes time because many of the stocks are still not cheap. He said the market’s key question is whether buyers stepping in at lower levels or sellers re‑evaluating long‑term prospects will dominate; Thursday’s trading suggests the latter effect was more pronounced.

items.title: 升息還沒完？Fed兩官員發聲 通膨仍是頭號風險
items.title_en: Rate Hikes Not Over? Two Fed Officials Warn Inflation Remains Top Risk
paras: 聯準會(Fed)兩名官員周四(5日)表示，為壓低通膨，貨幣政策仍有進一步緊縮的必要。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁哈瑪克(Beth Hammack)主張，在情況允許時採取更頻繁、小幅度的調整，避免政策落後；里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁巴金(Tom Barkin)則支持漸進升息，並指出通膨仍是當前最重要的風險。
綜合《彭博》與《CNBC》報導，Fed上周維持基準利率在3.75%至4%不變，但市場仍高度預期年底前再度升息。根據芝商所FedWatch工具，交易員預估12月升息機率超過80%，2027年還會再升一次。

哈瑪克主張小幅頻繁調整 避免通膨心態扎根

哈瑪克在瑞士蘇黎世一場活動的預備講稿中表示，貨幣政策需要轉向具有限制性的立場，才能讓通膨及時回到2%目標。她偏好在可行情況下，更頻繁地進行小幅調整，以降低政策落後及企業、消費者形成「通膨心態」的風險。
哈瑪克是上周反對維持利率不變的兩名官員之一。她指出，美國通膨高於目標已近六年，價格壓力相當廣泛，同時受到供給與需求因素影響。反覆出現的供給衝擊，也可能使企業與家庭習慣物價持續上漲，增加抗通膨難度。
相較之下，她對就業情勢的評估較為正面。美國勞動市場雖長期處於低招募、低裁員狀態，但她已看到一些可能略為轉強的跡象，認為Fed就業目標這一端的表現大致良好。

巴金支持漸進升息 認為目前政策接近中性

巴金同日在里奇蒙聯準銀行財務長峰會接受《CNBC》訪問時表示，失業率處於低檔、通膨卻過高，政策方向因此相對清楚，真正需要討論的是升息步調。他尚無法確定利率最終需要升至何處，或應以多快速度調整。
他認為，在全球充滿不確定性、等待期間又能取得更多資訊的情況下，漸進升息仍是合理做法。巴金今年並非聯邦公開市場委員會(FOMC)的投票委員，將於2027年取得投票權。
對目前政策立場，巴金認為利率接近既不刺激、也不抑制經濟的中性水準。不過，占美國經濟約三分之二的消費仍相對強勁，也可能意味政策略偏寬鬆，尚未明顯壓抑需求。
他強調，通膨是目前最重要的風險，希望9月升息及未來可能採取的行動，能對價格壓力產生影響。Fed在9月升息1碼時，官員大致認為年底前可能還需要再升息一次，但上周會議決定先等待更多資訊。

AI短期推升物價 融資風險可能藏在中介機構

巴金也將AI列為當前價格壓力的來源之一，但認為隨著時間推進，AI終將提高產出，協助緩解通膨。
另一方面，今年估計超過5,000億美元的大型雲端業者相關發債規模，也讓他關注潛在信用風險。
巴金表示，大型雲端業者的核心業務能創造龐大現金，因此很難直接認定這些公司的信用不佳。他更在意的是，哪些中介機構承擔了外界尚未掌握的風險，以及最大風險究竟集中在哪個環節。
兩名官員發言之際，民主黨剛在期中選舉取得國會兩院控制權，可能改變川普對Fed施壓的政治環境。哈瑪克強調，Fed的公信力來自依據證據與經濟數據制定政策，而非迎合短期政治壓力；這項公信力既有助維持低而穩定的通膨，也支撐美元的地位。
paras_en: Two Federal Reserve officials said on Thursday (the 5th) that further tightening of monetary policy is still needed to bring inflation down. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack advocates more frequent, smaller adjustments when conditions allow to avoid policy lag, while Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin backs a gradual rate‑hike path and says inflation remains the most important risk today.

According to Bloomberg and CNBC, the Fed left its target range unchanged at 3.75%‑4% last week, but markets still expect another hike before year‑end. The CME FedWatch tool shows traders assigning more than an 80% probability to a December increase and even a further hike in 2027.

Hammack argues for small, frequent tweaks to keep an inflation‑mindset from taking root. In a preparatory speech for an event in Zurich, she said monetary policy must shift to a more restrictive stance to bring inflation back to the 2% goal in a timely manner. When feasible, she prefers more frequent, modest adjustments to reduce the risk of policy lag and of businesses and consumers developing an “inflation mindset.”

Hammack was one of two officials who opposed keeping rates steady last week. She noted that U.S. inflation has been above target for almost six years, with price pressures broadly based and driven by both supply‑ and demand‑side factors. Repeated supply shocks could also cause firms and households to become accustomed to rising prices, making it harder to fight inflation.

By contrast, she is more upbeat on the labor market. Although the U.S. job market has long been characterized by low hiring and low layoffs, she sees some signs of a modest strengthening and believes the Fed’s employment side of the mandate is generally performing well.

Barkin, speaking to CNBC at the Richmond Fed’s finance chief summit, said that with unemployment low and inflation still too high, the policy direction is relatively clear and the real debate is about the pace of rate hikes. He cannot yet say how high rates ultimately need to go or how quickly adjustments should be made.

He argues that, given global uncertainty and the ability to gather more information over time, a gradual tightening remains sensible. Barkin is not a voting member of the Federal Open Market Committee this year and will gain voting rights in 2027.

Regarding the current stance, Barkin sees rates as close to a neutral level that neither stimulates nor restrains the economy. Yet about two‑thirds of U.S. economic activity—consumer spending—remains relatively strong, which could imply policy is slightly accommodative and has not yet noticeably dampened demand.

He stressed that inflation is the most important risk right now and hopes a September rate hike and any future actions will affect price pressures. When the Fed raises rates by a quarter point in September, officials generally think another hike may be needed before year‑end, but last week’s meeting decided to wait for more data.
Barkin also cited AI as a short‑term driver of price pressures, but believes that over time AI will boost output and help ease inflation.
On the other hand, he is watching potential credit risk from the more than $500 billion of bond issuance this year by large cloud‑service providers.

Barkin said the core businesses of big cloud firms generate massive cash flows, making it hard to label them as credit‑poor. What concerns him more is which intermediaries are bearing risks that are not yet fully understood and where the greatest risk concentration lies.

The officials’ remarks come as Democrats have just taken control of both chambers of Congress in the mid‑term elections, a shift that could change the political environment in which former President Trump pressures the Fed. Hammack emphasized that the Fed’s credibility comes from basing policy on evidence and economic data, not on short‑term political pressure; that credibility helps keep inflation low and stable and supports the dollar’s standing.

items.title: 南韓財團加速布局美國、縮減中國業務 10年內美國關係企業增至3.3倍
items.title_en: South Korean Conglomerates Accelerate U.S. Expansion, Shrink China Operations; U.S. Subsidiaries Triple in Ten Years
paras: 韓媒《Business Korea》報導，南韓財團正在加速布局美國，並縮減中國業務，目前美國關係企業加數已經增至10年前的3.3倍，而中國關係企業的數量則減少，顯示隨著美國保護主義升溫，關稅與補貼政策相繼出爐，在美國當地生產及確保供應鏈已成為企業布局的重要考量
企業資料研究機構CEO Score統計，不含HMM與酷澎(Coupang)，南韓28大企業集團的美國關係企業數量10年來從394家增至1,308家。相較之下，中國子公司數量從700家減至529家。
以南韓企業集團海外據點來看，10年前以中國占比最高，為23.1%，但今年美國以26.5%的占比躍居第一，中國比重大幅降至10.7%。
這項變化主要受到美國保護主義貿易政策推動。川普政府的關稅壓力，以及對中國產品加強監管，削弱企業在中國生產的成本優勢。相較之下，在美國當地生產，已成為企業降低關稅風險、穩定掌握主要客戶與供應鏈的方式。
一名南韓企業界高層說：「儘管美國共和黨與民主黨在政治上嚴重分歧，但在經濟安全方面，兩黨具有跨黨派的共同觀點。以美國為中心整頓企業布局的趨勢，可望延續下去。」

韓五大集團加碼美國 韓華增加最多

三星、SK、現代汽車、LG與韓華等五大集團，過去10年的美國子公司數量大增648家，從2016年的240家增至今年的888家。
這當中布局最積極的是韓華集團，其在美國的關係企業從2016年的63家增加至今年的374家，增加311家，增幅為五大集團之冠。這主要是由韓華解決方案(Hanwha Solutions)擴大太陽能生產與銷售業務、韓華能源(Hanwha Energy)拓展能源儲存系統(ESS)業務，以及韓華海洋與韓華系統收購美國費城造船廠(Philly Shipyard)等因素帶動。
SK集團的美國關係企業則從10年前的40家增加至243家，反映SK On擴大美國電池業務等措施。
三星集團在美國的關係企業數量從52家增至95家。三星在2017年收購美國汽車電子與音響專業廠商Harman後，旗下美國據點數量大幅增加，三星SDI與美國汽車製造商Stellantis及通用汽車(GM-US)推動電池合資事業也是原因之一。
南韓電池商正全面進軍美國ESS市場。LG能源解決方案也與通用汽車及本田成立合資企業，鎖定北美電池市場。受此帶動，樂金集團的美國子公司從30家增加至64家。
現代汽車集團則透過在美國喬治亞州興建工廠強化當地生產布局，以及持續投資新事業，包括收購波士頓動力(Boston Dynamics)，以及成立先進空中運輸公司Supernal。現代汽車集團在美國的關係企業數量因此從55家增至112家。

南韓企業調整中國布局 三星與LG縮減產能

中國過去憑藉低廉勞動力成本，扮演「世界工廠」的角色。但如今，南韓企業正在中國市場針對不同業務推動整頓，使五大集團在中國的子公司數量從330家減至269家。
三星電子關閉在中國的智慧型手機生產設施，LG顯示(LG Display)則出售位於廣州的液晶顯示器(LCD)工廠。
paras_en: South Korean media outlet Business Korea reports that Korean conglomerates are accelerating their U.S. expansion while reducing their China operations. The number of U.S.-related subsidiaries has risen to 3.3 times what it was ten years ago, while the number of China-related subsidiaries has decreased, reflecting the impact of rising U.S. protectionism, tariffs, and subsidy policies that make local production and supply‑chain security key considerations for companies.

According to CEO Score, a corporate data research firm, excluding HMM and Coupang, the number of U.S. subsidiaries among Korea’s 28 major conglomerates grew from 394 to 1,308 over the past decade. In contrast, the number of Chinese subsidiaries fell from 700 to 529.
Looking at overseas footprints, China accounted for the largest share 10 years ago at 23.1%, but this year the U.S. leads with 26.5%, while China’s share dropped sharply to 10.7%.

This shift is largely driven by U.S. protectionist trade policies. The Trump administration’s tariff pressure and tighter regulation of Chinese products eroded the cost advantage of producing in China. Local U.S. production has become a way for companies to reduce tariff risk and stabilize relationships with major customers and supply chains.

A senior Korean business executive said, "Although the Republican and Democratic parties are deeply divided politically, they share bipartisan views on economic security. The trend of restructuring corporate layouts around the U.S. is likely to continue."
The five largest Korean conglomerates—Samsung, SK, Hyundai Motor, LG, and Hanwha—have added 648 U.S. subsidiaries over the past decade, rising from 240 in 2016 to 888 this year.

Hanwha Group has been the most aggressive, increasing its U.S. subsidiaries from 63 in 2016 to 374 this year—a gain of 311 and the highest among the five groups. This surge is driven by Hanwha Solutions expanding solar production and sales, Hanwha Energy expanding energy‑storage‑system (ESS) business, and Hanwha Marine and Hanwha Systems acquiring the Philadelphia Shipyard in the U.S. in 2024.
SK Group’s U.S. subsidiaries grew from 40 ten years ago to 243, reflecting SK On’s expansion of U.S. battery business and related initiatives.

Samsung Group’s U.S. subsidiaries rose from 52 to 95. Samsung’s acquisition of U.S. automotive electronics and audio specialist Harman in 2017 greatly increased its U.S. presence, and Samsung SDI’s joint ventures with U.S. automakers Stellantis and General Motors (GM‑US) also contributed.

South Korean battery makers are fully entering the U.S. ESS market. LG Energy Solution has formed joint ventures with GM and Honda to target the North American battery market. As a result, LG’s U.S. subsidiaries grew from 30 to 64.

Hyundai Motor Group has strengthened its local production footprint by building a factory in Georgia, U.S., and continues to invest in new ventures, including the acquisition of Boston Dynamics and the creation of the advanced aerial transport company Supernal. Consequently, Hyundai Motor Group’s U.S. subsidiaries increased from 55 to 112.

South Korean companies are adjusting their China strategy. Samsung and LG are reducing capacity. China, once a low‑cost labor hub and the "world factory," is now seeing Korean firms reorganize their operations. The five largest conglomerates’ Chinese subsidiaries fell from 330 to 269.
Samsung Electronics shut down its smartphone manufacturing facility in China, and LG Display sold its LCD factory in Guangzhou.

paras: 中央銀行今(5)日公布10月底我國外匯存底金額為5964.37億美元，月減 43.08億美元，跌破6000億美元關卡，創3個月來低點，央行指出，10月外資淨匯出約280億美元(含盈餘匯出)創單月新高，折合新台幣約9000億元，因此為維持外匯市場秩序，有進場調節阻貶，使新台幣單月僅貶值2.29%。

央行強調，不會刻意改變匯市方向，但不樂見看到匯率波動太大，會有一些調節以維持動態穩定。
此外，央行統計主要國家的外匯存底，中國降至3兆4003億美元，日本也降至9769億美元，印度為5932億美元，南韓為4187億美元。
對於新台幣近期貶值甚至在今日觸及33元整數大關，央行表示，廠商可能有所期待，但「不認為它會一直持續下去」，也表態「希望大家主要是實質拋補，不要有太大一個期待」，並重申「希望年底前廠商的結匯需求能夠多出來一點」的立場。
paras_en: The central bank announced today (the 5th) that Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves stood at $5,964.37 billion at the end of October, a monthly decline of $4.308 billion, slipping below the $6 trillion threshold and hitting a three‑month low. The bank noted that net foreign capital outflows in October amounted to about $28 billion (including profit repatriation), a record high for a single month, equivalent to roughly NT$9 trillion. To maintain order in the FX market, the bank stepped in to curb further depreciation, limiting the New Taiwan dollar’s monthly loss to just 2.29%.

According to the central bank’s calculations, foreign investors’ holdings of domestic stocks and bonds, valued at market prices and combined with their New Taiwan dollar deposits, totalled about $1.7426 trillion, which is roughly 292% of the foreign exchange reserves—a low not seen since May.

The central bank emphasized that it will not deliberately steer the exchange‑rate direction, but it is uneasy about excessive volatility and will make adjustments as needed to preserve dynamic stability.

In addition, the bank’s statistics on major countries’ foreign exchange reserves show China’s reserves falling to $3.4003 trillion, Japan’s to $976.9 billion, India’s at $593.2 billion, and South Korea’s at $418.7 billion.

Regarding the recent depreciation of the New Taiwan dollar, which even touched the round figure of 33 NT$ today, the central bank said that while market participants might have expectations, "we do not believe it will continue indefinitely." It urged firms to focus on real hedging rather than harboring large expectations and reiterated its hope that firms’ settlement‑demand for foreign exchange will increase before year‑end.

items.title: 挪威央行維持利率4.5%不變 總裁仍警告通膨過高 保留升息選項
items.title_en: Norway Central Bank Keeps Rate at 4.5% as Governor Warns Inflation Still Too High, Leaves Rate‑Hike Option Open
paras: 挪威央行周四(5日)將基準存款利率維持在4.5%的高點不變，符合媒體調查中分析師的預測，然而，央行政策制定者重申，若有需要抑止通膨，仍保留再次升息的選項。
針對利率政策與物價前景，挪威央行總裁Ida Wolden Bache在官方聲明中表示通膨過高。他進一步強調：「政策利率可能需要在一段時間內保持高位，若需要將通膨率降至目標，我們已準備好調升政策利率。」
雖然這個富含能源的國家在夏季的通膨放緩超乎預期，但官員們仍面臨全面平抑物價成長的挑戰。自2022年以來，挪威通膨持續顯著高於目標，部分原因係央行優先考慮維持低失業率，官方目前預估要到2029年才能實現2%的通膨目標。
在國內經濟方面，由於本土經濟持續擴張，薪資壓力僅漸進放緩，少數派工黨內閣在與盟友協商後的明年預算可能更具擴張性，為物價添增上行壓力。然而，挪威克朗今年做為G10國家中表現最強勁者，貨幣走高正降低進口通膨的風險。
經濟學家指出，克朗走強可能讓挪威利率制定者在本輪周期免於額外升息，儘管投資人仍反映明年3月會議升息機率約有50%。
與此同時，全球其他央行正積極進行緊縮。鄰國瑞典央行周三實施了自2023年以來的首次升息，市場廣泛預期英國央行將在周四稍晚調升利率。
paras_en: On Thursday (the 5th), Norway’s central bank kept its policy deposit rate unchanged at the high level of 4.5%, matching analysts’ expectations in media surveys. However, policymakers reiterated that they still retain the option to raise rates again if needed to curb inflation.

Regarding rate policy and price outlook, Norges Bank Governor Ida Wolden Bache said in an official statement that inflation remains too high. She added, “The policy rate may need to stay elevated for a period of time; if we need to bring inflation down to target, we are ready to raise the policy rate further.”

Although this energy‑rich country saw summer inflation ease more than expected, officials still face the challenge of broadly tempering price growth. Since 2022, Norwegian inflation has stayed well above target, partly because the central bank has prioritized keeping unemployment low. The authorities now estimate that the 2% inflation goal will not be reached until 2029.

Domestically, the economy continues to expand and wage pressures are only gradually easing. A minority‑led Labour government, after negotiations with its coalition partners, may present a more expansionary budget for next year, adding upward pressure on prices. Meanwhile, the Norwegian krone has been the strongest performer among G10 currencies this year, and its appreciation is reducing the risk of imported inflation.

Economists note that a stronger krone could spare Norway’s rate‑setters from needing an additional hike in this cycle, although investors still price roughly a 50% chance of a rate increase at the March meeting next year.

At the same time, other central banks around the world are actively tightening. Neighboring Sweden’s central bank implemented its first rate hike since 2023 on Wednesday, and markets widely expect the Bank of England to raise rates later on Thursday.

items.title: 新台幣要逢低反轉了？外匯局長對近期匯市給這些說法
items.title_en: Is the New Taiwan Dollar Set to Reverse on Lows? The Central Bank's Forex Chief Comments on Recent Market Moves
paras: 新台幣今(5)日爆出成交天量，台北外匯經紀公司成交值衝上36.56億美元，最低也一度貶至32.985元，創去年4月以來新低，中央銀行外匯局長蔡烱民表示，匯價本是動態調整，「沒有什麼數字才是合不合理」，但也強調，「有感覺外資賣超已有收斂情形」，且「年底前國內廠商會出來進行結售，不會一直持續下去」；外界解讀，央行在帶頭信心喊話。
蔡烱民表示，近期外資賣超幅度和11月跌點，數據拿來對照10月跌點，其實近日外資賣超有在收斂情形，不過，「只是一個趨勢，還不是很一定，央行會密切觀察變動情形」。
蔡烱民強調，新台幣貶值最主要還是反映外資匯出，「波動大都是不好的」，央行會關注匯市供需是否平衡，並再次指出，台灣基本面和國際收支都非常好，今年以來至今新台幣貶值因素約4%左右，跟過去相比並非很特別的幅度，只是比較集中在最近，才讓市場有感。
蔡烱民進一步提及，時序近年底，廠商須有所結算，「年底前會出來結售，就不會一直持續下去，觀察到這幾天廠商賣匯金額有增加」。
同時，蔡烱民認為，「外資一旦回頭，力道也會非常高」。
paras_en: The New Taiwan dollar saw a massive trading volume today (the 5th), with a Taipei foreign‑exchange brokerage reporting a transaction value of US$3.656 billion and the rate briefly slipping to NT$32.985, the lowest since April last year. Central Bank Foreign Exchange Director Cai Jung‑min said the exchange rate is naturally dynamic – “there’s no single number that is unreasonable” – but noted that “it feels like foreign‑capital net selling is already easing” and that “domestic firms will settle and unwind positions before year‑end, so the decline won’t continue indefinitely,” a statement interpreted as the central bank trying to boost confidence.

Cai explained that the recent net‑selling by foreign investors and the November dip, when compared with the October dip, show that foreign‑capital outflows have been narrowing lately. However, he cautioned that this is only a trend and not yet certain, adding that the central bank will closely monitor any changes.

He emphasized that the main driver of the NT$ depreciation is foreign‑capital outflows and that “large volatility is undesirable.” The central bank will watch whether supply and demand in the FX market remain balanced, and reiterated that Taiwan’s fundamentals and external balances are very strong. So far this year, the NT$ has weakened by about 4%, which is not a particularly large move historically; the recent concentration of that decline is what the market is feeling.

Cai added that, as we approach year‑end, companies will need to settle their positions. “They will come out to settle and unwind before the end of the year, so the downward pressure won’t persist, and we have observed an increase in the amount of foreign‑exchange sold by firms in the past few days,” he said.
He also said that “once foreign investors turn back, their buying power will be very strong.”

items.title: 1958年來最慘！《紐約客》評共和黨崩盤：美國的復仇、對川普的否決
items.title_en: The Worst Since 1958! The New Yorker Says the GOP Crumbled: America’s Revenge and a Veto on Trump
paras: 2026年美國期中選舉以一場對現任總統所在政黨的「毀滅性打擊」落幕。民主黨橫掃國會，多個傳統紅州翻藍。這場被視為對川普及其政策「全民公投」的選舉，引發白宮劇烈震盪。總統川普拒絕承擔責任，副總統范斯則罕見承認選民倒戈的殘酷現實。
《紐約客》雜誌專欄作家Susan B. Glasser週三(4日)撰文指出，選舉之夜未過晚上11點，川普才首次發聲。過去幾週，他堅稱選舉是對其個人的公投，但面對慘敗，他第一時間在社群媒體推卸責任：「我不在選票上，如果我在，我們肯定會大獲全勝！」
隨後，他指責德州州長阿博特變成「名義上的共和黨人」，還抱怨《福斯新聞》「不斷播放民主黨反對節目」。
週三早上，川普接受《福斯新聞》採訪時仍堅稱「我不應感到內疚」，白宮隨後還發布川普坐在堅毅桌後的照片，並配上一行文字：「重要提示：川普仍是你們的總統」，試圖強調其執政合法性。
與川普否認形成對比的是，范斯週三早上承認：「主要問題是，許多在2024年投票給川普跟范斯的人，今年卻投給民主黨，他甚至將敗因歸咎於伊朗戰爭，稱「我們失敗的原因就是這場戰爭」。
文中指出，此次選舉是自1974年尼克森下台前，美國總統遭遇到的最徹底否決的一場大選。共和黨在眾議院恐失至少35席，參議院失去多達8席，規模僅見於1958年。選民不滿情緒強烈且多元，普通共和黨選民表達了對川普政策及政黨的「道德厭惡」。
除伊朗戰爭外，柴油價格逼近每加侖7美元、關稅與貿易戰、背叛烏克蘭、政府官員自我斂財、資料中心擴張以及馬斯克等富豪干預選舉，均成為選民投票反對的理由。
川普最後一個月的競選活動，21天內舉行21場集會，大談奇怪話題，並貶低選民對住房負擔能力的擔憂，更被指加劇了選民疏離。
儘管川普試圖將失敗歸咎於一切外部因素，但他私下告訴《紐約時報》，他「絕對願意」接受選舉結果。這場選舉不僅重塑了華府權力格局，更成為美國選民對川普時代的一次清晰清算。
paras_en: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections ended with a "devastating blow" to the incumbent president’s party. Democrats swept Congress, flipping several traditional red states blue. The election, seen as a nationwide referendum on Trump and his policies, sent shockwaves through the White House. President Trump refused to take responsibility, while Vice President Pence unusually acknowledged the harsh reality of voters defecting.

New Yorker columnist Susan B. Glasser wrote on Wednesday (the 4th) that Trump did not speak until after 11 p.m. on election night. In the weeks leading up to the vote he had insisted the election was a personal referendum, but after the crushing loss he immediately shifted blame on social media: "I’m not on the ballot; if I were, we would have won hands down!"
He then blamed Texas Governor Abbott for becoming a "nominal Republican" and complained that Fox News was "continuously airing anti‑Democratic programming."

On Wednesday morning, Trump told Fox News that he "should not feel guilty," and the White House later released a photo of him seated behind a sturdy desk with the caption: "Important note: Trump is still your president," attempting to underscore his legitimacy.

In contrast, Pence on Wednesday morning admitted: "The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump and me in 2024 voted for the Democrats this year," and even blamed the loss on the Iran war, saying, "The reason we lost is this war."

The article notes this election is the most thorough repudiation of a U.S. president since Nixon’s resignation in 1974. Republicans risk losing at least 35 seats in the House and up to eight in the Senate, a scale not seen since 1958. Voter anger is strong and diverse, with ordinary GOP voters expressing "moral disgust" toward Trump’s policies and the party.

Beyond the Iran war, factors such as diesel prices nearing $7 per gallon, tariffs and trade wars, perceived betrayal of Ukraine, officials enriching themselves, data‑center expansion, and interventions by billionaires like Elon Musk all motivated voters to cast anti‑Trump ballots.
In his final month of campaigning, Trump held 21 rallies in 21 days, spouting odd topics, dismissing voters’ concerns about housing affordability, and was accused of deepening voter alienation.

Although Trump tried to blame everything on external factors, he privately told the New York Times that he is "absolutely willing" to accept the election results. The vote not only reshaped the power dynamics in Washington but also served as a clear reckoning by American voters of the Trump era.

U.S. job openings surged in September by 333,000 to 7.523 million, while layoffs fell by 127,000 to 1.641 million – the lowest since March last year – indicating a still‑solid labor market. President Trump told the Financial Times the U.S. has no plan to strike Iran, but senior Iranian officials said a peace deal was far off, sparking sharp oil‑price swings. Investors, weighing Middle‑East tensions and the U.S. mid‑term election outcome, remained cautious, pushing the dollar against the yen down from the 158.74 high on Wednesday. As markets bet the Democrats would wrest control of Congress from Trump’s Republicans, concerns about political gridlock, restrained fiscal spending and tougher AI regulation weighed on growth, extending the dollar‑yen decline to a 157.39 low.

Later, credit‑rating agency Scope Ratings said the Democrats’ sweep in the U.S. mid‑terms was positive for sovereign credit, keeping the rating at AA‑ with a stable outlook. ADP’s national employment report showed private‑sector jobs rose by 86,000 in October, and the Commerce Department reported September’s trade deficit narrowed to $105 billion, better than expected. S&P Global data showed U.S. composite and services PMI final values fell to 55.9 and 56.1, while ISM’s non‑manufacturing PMI slipped to 54.5, still above the 50 growth threshold. Combined with still‑high inflation, the dollar regained some strength against the yen. The dollar‑yen resistance is projected around 158.30‑158.50, support around 157.30‑157.50 today.
EUR/USD

New Zealand’s Q3 unemployment rate rose to an eleven‑year high of 5.7% and employment fell 0.1% from the previous quarter, cutting the RBNZ’s odds of a December rate hike to 57% and hurting the kiwi. Australian data showed September household spending rose 0.6% month‑over‑month, above expectations and flat year‑over‑year, but October’s seasonally‑adjusted Chinese services PMI fell to a three‑month low of 50.8, pressuring the Aussie and other risk currencies and pulling the euro‑dollar down to a 1.1183 low.

Subsequent S&P Global October PMI final values for France fell to 46.6 (composite) and 46.2 (services), the fastest contraction in five months, while Germany’s fell to 53.4 and 52.5. Euro‑area PMI hit four‑month lows of 51.7 and 51.4, yet October euro‑area inflation rose to a three‑year high of 4.0%, bolstering expectations of further ECB hikes. Bundesbank President Nagel said the ECB will almost certainly raise rates again in December. The Democrats’ strong win of both chambers sparked short covering of euro shorts ahead of the election, lifting the euro‑dollar to a 1.1272 peak. items.title: 共和黨敗選後首波政治清算！赫格塞斯成美伊戰爭「替罪羔羊」 CNN：最快下周啟動彈劾投票
items.title_en: First Wave of Political Payback After GOP Election Loss! Hegseth Becomes the “Scapegoat” of the US‑Iran War, CNN: Impeachment Vote Could Start as Early as Next Week
paras: 美國期中選舉民主黨橫掃參眾兩院，共和黨內迅速掀起問責風暴，矛頭直指國防部長赫格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)，最新傳出多位共和黨議員與盟友將敗選歸咎於伊朗戰爭，認為赫格塞斯是推動開戰的關鍵人物，卻未規劃退場機制與政治後果管理。
《CNN》報導，肯塔基州共和黨籍眾議員Thomas Massie在眾議院復會後，將發起彈劾赫格塞思的投票，指控其未經國會授權對伊朗採取敵對行動、濫用職權。共和黨消息人士預期表決可過關，這將是現屆國會選後首波政治清算。
美國總統川普週三(4日)則公開力挺赫格塞斯，稱其「幹得非常好」、無意撤換，但顧問私下坦言，戰爭拖累選情下，「總得有人承擔責任，而不會是總統」。
美國副總統萬斯亦鬆口質疑伊朗戰事是否值得，共和黨參議員Thom Tillis直言赫格塞斯終將面臨「清算」，其與國會交惡更恐拖累1.5兆美元國防支出案。
民主黨已承諾展開廣泛調查，涵蓋伊朗軍事行動決策、高階將領「清洗」、烏克蘭政策，以及拉美海域疑似涉戰爭罪的反毒空襲。
另有傳聞稱，赫格塞斯可能轉任田納西州參議員，接替明年出任州長的Marsha Blackburn遺缺，川普僅稱「沒聽說過這種說法」。
分析指出，2006年小布希以倫斯斐為伊拉克戰爭背書的下課劇本正被重提。赫格塞思雖暫保官位，卻同時承受白宮止損、黨內倒戈、國會調查三重壓力，這場「替罪羔羊」博弈，將決定川普政府剩餘任期的國防路線與戰爭責任歸屬。
paras_en: The Democrats swept both houses of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections, prompting an immediate accountability storm within the Republican Party that zeroes in on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Multiple GOP lawmakers and allies are blaming the loss on the war with Iran, arguing that Hegseth was the key figure who pushed the country into conflict without a clear exit strategy or political fallout management plan.

CNN reports that Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky will launch an impeachment vote against Hegseth after the House reconvenes, accusing him of taking hostile action against Iran without congressional authorization and abusing his authority. Republican sources expect the vote to pass, marking the first wave of political payback in the current Congress after the election.

President Donald Trump publicly backed Hegseth on Wednesday (the 4th), calling his performance “very good” and saying there is no intention to replace him. However, advisers privately admitted that the war is hurting the administration’s electoral prospects and that “someone has to take responsibility, and it won’t be the president.”

Vice President Kamala Harris also hinted that the Iran war may not be worth it, while Republican Senator Thom Tillis bluntly said Hegseth will eventually face “payback,” warning that his clash with Congress could jeopardize a $1.5 trillion defense spending bill.

Democrats have pledged a broad investigation covering the decision‑making behind Iran’s military actions, a “purge” of senior officers, Ukraine policy, and alleged war‑crime‑related anti‑drug airstrikes in Latin American waters.

There are rumors that Hegseth could be appointed to the U.S. Senate from Tennessee to fill the seat that will be vacated by Governor‑elect Marsha Blackburn next year; Trump said he “has never heard of such a suggestion.”

Analysts note that the script used in 2006 when George W. Bush backed the Iraq war with the Lunsford‑type resignation is being revisited. While Hegseth currently retains his post, he is simultaneously under pressure from the White House to cut losses, from his party’s internal revolt, and from congressional investigations. This “scapegoat” showdown will determine the defense trajectory and war‑responsibility allocation for the remainder of the Trump administration’s term.

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉民主黨拿下參眾兩院、掃除選舉不確定性 美元走軟
items.title_en: New York FX Market: Democrats Capture Both Chambers, Removing Election Uncertainty, Dollar Weakens
paras: 美元對主要貨幣周三(4日)走軟，民主黨在美國期中選舉大獲全勝，拿下參眾兩院，掃除市場原本可能因選舉爭議所面臨的巨大不確定性，投資人同時也在權衡監管政策改變的可能性。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣走勢的ICE美元指數(DXY)下跌0.25%，報101.60，盤中稍早曾跌至101.21，創9月30日以來最低。
歐元兌美元升值0.21%至1.1217美元，稍早曾升至1.1272美元，是10月6日以來最高。
民主黨掌控美國參議院與眾議院，在部分共和黨傳統票倉取得數十年來首見的壓倒性勝利，數千萬選民以選票嚴厲譴責總統川普。
這場大勝緩解了外界對選舉結果可能引發爭議的疑慮，但也讓美國面臨分裂政府與立法僵局的可能性：共和黨掌控白宮，民主黨則掌控國會，時間正值美國設法因應伊朗戰爭，以及同時推動經濟成長、加劇通膨的人工智慧(AI)熱潮。
美股周三應聲上漲，標普500指數上漲約2%。投資人等待華府對美國與以色列對伊朗戰爭的下一步行動之際，原油價格則大幅下挫。
多倫多貴金屬交易商Silver Gold Bull外匯與貴金屬風險管理主管Erik Bregar說：「市場瀰漫風險偏好情緒。或許我們看到的是一種『利多出盡後賣出、事實明朗後買進』的組合，也就是市場對選舉結果不會因舞弊爭議而陷入僵局感到寬慰。」
他說：「從基本面來看，民主黨對資料中心等議題的立場，仍可能讓市場對AI產生更多疑慮。但就目前而言，市場鬆了一口氣，因為川普不會對選舉結果提出抗爭。當各類資產普遍呈現風險偏好情緒時，通常會對美元造成壓力。」
儘管美國政局出現變化，市場對聯準會(Fed)利率走向的預期大致維持不變。根據芝商所(CME Group)FedWatch工具，市場目前預估，Fed 12月會議升息至少1碼的機率為81.2%，高於前一交易日的77.4%。

就業數據優於預期

ADP全美私人企業就業報告顯示，美國民間企業10月新增8.6萬個工作機會，高於經濟學家預估的6.9萬個。這是本周陸續公布的一系列勞動市場數據之一，重頭戲將是周五由美國政府公布的非農就業報告。
美國供應管理協會(ISM)另一份報告則顯示，10月非製造業指數從9月的54.9降至54.5。最新數值略低於經濟學家預估的54.8，但仍高於代表景氣擴張的50榮枯線。
在英格蘭銀行(BOE，央行)周四公布利率決策前，英鎊上揚0.38%至1.3462美元，英鎊盤中一度升至1.3503美元，創逾七周新高。
這是英鎊連續第六個交易日升值，將是自7月6日結束連八日漲勢以來最長的連漲紀錄。
市場預期，英國央行將因能源成本飆升帶來的通膨壓力而升息，但可能反駁投資人對明年還會有數次升息的押注。

paras_en: The dollar weakened against major currencies on Wednesday (the 4th) as the Democratic Party achieved a sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections, taking control of both the Senate and the House and eliminating the huge uncertainty that markets had faced over possible election disputes. Investors are also weighing the likelihood of regulatory policy changes.

In the New York close, the ICE Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, fell 0.25% to 101.60 after dipping earlier in the session to 101.21, its lowest level since September 30.
The euro rose 0.21% against the dollar to $1.1217, having earlier peaked at $1.1272, the highest since October 6.

The Democrats now control the U.S. Senate and House, winning an overwhelming victory in several traditional Republican strongholds for the first time in decades, with tens of millions of voters harshly rebuking President Trump at the ballot box.

The landslide eases concerns that the election outcome could spark disputes, but it also raises the prospect of a divided government and legislative gridlock: Republicans hold the White House while Democrats control Congress, at a time when the U.S. must respond to the Iran war and simultaneously drive economic growth amid an AI-fueled inflation surge.
U.S. equities rose on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 up about 2%. While investors await Washington’s next steps on the Iran conflict involving the United States and Israel, oil prices fell sharply.

Erik Bregar, head of FX and precious‑metal risk management at Toronto‑based Silver Gold Bull, said, “The market is awash with risk‑on sentiment. Perhaps we are seeing a ‘sell after the news is fully priced in, buy once the facts are clear’ mix, meaning the market is relieved that the election result will not be mired in fraud disputes.”

He added, “From a fundamentals view, the Democrats’ stance on data‑center issues and the like could still raise more AI‑related concerns. But for now the market has breathed a sigh of relief because Trump is unlikely to contest the result. When assets broadly show risk‑on sentiment, the dollar usually comes under pressure.”

Despite the political shift, expectations for the Federal Reserve’s rate path remain largely unchanged. According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, the market now sees an 81.2% probability that the Fed will raise rates by at least one basis point at the December meeting, up from 77.4% the previous trading day.

Employment data beat expectations. The ADP National Employment Report showed private‑sector employers added 86,000 jobs in October, above economists’ forecast of 69,000. This is one of several labor‑market releases this week, with the headline non‑farm payroll report due from the U.S. government on Friday.

A separate ISM report showed the October non‑manufacturing index fell to 54.5 from September’s 54.9. The reading was slightly below the 54.8 forecast but remained well above the 50‑point threshold that signals expansion.
Ahead of the Bank of England’s (BOE) Thursday rate decision, the pound rose 0.38% to $1.3462, briefly reaching $1.3503 intraday – a seven‑week high.
This marks the pound’s sixth consecutive trading‑day gain, the longest streak since the eight‑day rally that ended on July 6.
Markets expect the BOE to raise rates in response to inflation pressure from soaring energy costs, though this may counter investors’ bets on multiple hikes next year.
The dollar slipped 0.14% against the yen, trading at ¥158.43.

items.title: 美國民主黨勝選預期引爆避險潮 日股暴跌 日元走升
items.title_en: Democratic Victory Expected in U.S. Triggers Safe‑Haven Rally, Japanese Stocks Plunge, Yen Rises
paras: 受美國期中選舉開票序盤顯示民主黨居於優勢影響，市場擔憂人工智慧(AI)與資料中心可能面臨更嚴格的法規監管，引發日本市場周三(4日)出現強烈避險情緒。
日股周三跌勢於午後擴大，日經平均指數一度大跌逾2,800點，跌幅達4.6%，下探60,206點，跌破被視為關鍵支撐的200日移動平均線61,880。東證指數(TOPIX)同樣重挫3.3%。相較於股市受創，匯市則湧入避險買盤，美元遭遇拋售，日元兌美元升值0.7%至157.65附近。
本輪賣壓集中於AI與半導體類股，愛德萬測試(Advantest)一度重挫9.6%、軟銀集團(SoftBank Group)大跌10%，鎧俠(Kioxia)暴跌15%。賣壓並擴散至商社、機械及金融等類股。
SMBC信託銀行投資調查部長山口真弘分析指出，日股先前因企業財報強勁獲買盤支撐，加上前一日適逢日本國定假日休市，導致投資人進行補跌平倉，以及信用交易籌碼面不佳，加劇了賣壓。
針對市場焦慮，機構法人看法分歧。野村資產管理首席策略師石黑英之認為，當前走跌屬投機資金根據「民主黨交易」進行的機械式拋售，市場過度焦慮且過於短視。他指出，AI發展攸關美中霸權爭奪，趨勢難以止步，隨著企業基本面維持強勁，加上空頭回補，後續股價有望回升。
大和資產管理首席策略師建部和禮表示，眾議院過半已在預期中，焦點在於參議院開票。若民主黨僅微幅控制參議院，賣壓將於短期結束；若大勝過半，AI逆風恐將延續更長時間。
在匯市與展望方面，SMBC日興證券資深策略師丸山凜途指出，雖然民主黨優勢推升日元至157關卡附近，但考量美中競爭與總統否決權，嚴格規制難以實施，美元賣壓終將反轉。
藍天銀行首席市場策略師諸我晃補充，若民主黨奪下兩院，初期市場反應為避險與美元走弱，但當前美元拋售亦受到美股期指疲軟與中東地緣局勢緩和等因素影響。
paras_en: The market, worried that artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers could face tighter regulatory oversight, reacted to early mid‑term election results showing a Democratic advantage, sparking strong safe‑haven sentiment in Japan on Wednesday (the 4th).

Japanese equities fell sharply in the afternoon, with the Nikkei index at one point dropping more than 2,800 points—a 4.6% decline—to as low as 60,206, slipping below the key 200‑day moving average support of 61,880. The TOPIX also plunged 3.3%. In contrast, the currency market saw a rush of safe‑haven buying, the dollar was sold off and the yen rose about 0.7% to around 157.65 per dollar.

The sell‑off was concentrated in AI and semiconductor stocks, with Advantest tumbling 9.6%, SoftBank Group falling 10% and Kioxia plunging 15%. The pressure spread to trading houses, machinery and financial stocks as well.

SMBC Trust Bank’s head of investment research, Masahiro Yamaguchi, said the market had previously been supported by strong corporate earnings and, after a Japanese national holiday the day before, investors were forced to cover falling positions and weak margin‑trading balances, intensifying the sell pressure.

Institutional views diverged on the market anxiety. Nomura Asset Management chief strategist Hideyuki Ishiguro argued that the current decline is a mechanical sell‑off by speculative money reacting to a “Democratic trade,” and that the market is overly anxious and short‑sighted. He noted that AI development is tied to U.S.–China rivalry, the trend is hard to stop, and with solid corporate fundamentals and short covering, stocks could rebound.

Daiwa Asset Management chief strategist Kazuhide Kenbo said that the House of Representatives already being expected to tilt Democratic is only part of the story; the focus now is the Senate count. If Democrats only gain a slim Senate majority, the sell‑off should end soon; if they win a large majority, the AI headwind could persist longer.

Regarding FX and outlook, SMBC Nikko Securities senior strategist Rinto Maruyama pointed out that although the Democratic advantage has pushed the yen toward the 157 level, given U.S.–China competition and presidential veto power, strict regulation is unlikely to be implemented, and dollar‑selling pressure will eventually reverse.

Blue Sky Bank chief market strategist Sho Wataru added that if Democrats take control of both chambers, the initial market reaction will be safe‑haven buying and a weaker dollar, but the current dollar sell‑off is also being driven by weak U.S. equity futures and easing Middle‑East geopolitical tensions.
